# Habakkuk

::: {.book-summary}
## Book Summary Insight

Habakkuk wrestles with God's justice and learns to trust His sovereign purposes. The book teaches that the righteous live by faith even when circumstances remain confusing.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 1

<div class="key-verse">Habakkuk 1:5</div>

<div class="identifier">Behold among the nations, and wonder</div>

### Why This Verse

Quoted in Acts 13

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Habakkuk's questions about injustice and God's surprising answer. The key verse highlights the prophet's struggle to understand why God permits evil and how He chooses to address it.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 2

<div class="key-verse">Habakkuk 2:4</div>

<div class="identifier">The just shall live by faith</div>

### Why This Verse

One of the most important verses in the Bible

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains God's response concerning judgment and faith. The key verse teaches that the righteous live by faith, trusting God even when His plans are not fully understood.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 3

<div class="key-verse">Habakkuk 3:17</div>

<div class="identifier">Though the fig tree shall not blossom</div>

### Why This Verse

Famous declaration of faith

### Chapter Insight

This chapter is Habakkuk's prayer of praise and trust. The key verse expresses steadfast faith in God despite the loss of every visible source of security and blessing.
:::
